name: Zerah
overview: Zerah is a male Edomite figure noted in Scripture as the son of Reuel and a chief of Edom. His identity is grounded in his tribal affiliation with the Edomites and his leadership role within that community, as recorded in Genesis 36. There are no additional notes expanding on his life or character.
namesAndTitles: The name Zerah means 'dawning, shining or flashing [red or scarlet] light,' reflecting a vivid and possibly symbolic meaning in Hebrew. This proper name was not given directly by God but is recorded in the biblical text of Genesis 36.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture explicitly identifies Zerah as the son of Reuel, establishing a clear paternal relationship. Beyond this, no further family connections are documented in the biblical record for Zerah.
scriptureSignificance: Zerah holds significance as a chief of Edom, indicating a position of leadership and authority within the Edomite nation. His mention as the son of Reuel ties him to the genealogical records that outline the descent and leadership structure of Edom. This situates Zerah within the broader biblical narrative of the descendants of Esau and their role in the unfolding history of God's people.
